shipped_row.boundary_rationale: The unit opens the words-of-the-wise collection with a double attention-imperative, הַ֥ט אָזְנְךָ֗ (oshb:Prov.22.17, 'turn your ear'), paired with וּ֭שְׁמַע (oshb:Prov.22.17, 'and listen'), and the phrase דִּבְרֵ֣י חֲכָמִ֑ים (oshb:Prov.22.17, 'words of the wise') sits mid-verse rather than as a separate header line, so the seam is argued from the clause itself and not from a title. Verse 19 states the address's purpose in an infinitive clause, לִהְי֣וֹת בַּ֭יהוָה (oshb:Prov.22.19, 'so that your trust may be in Yahweh'), and verses 20-21 restate that purpose with two further purpose infinitives, לְהוֹדִֽיעֲךָ֗ and לְהָשִׁ֥יב (oshb:Prov.22.21). The unit closes with a petuchah/pe seg (oshb:Prov.22.21, single-witness), corroborating the move into the content admonitions that open at 22:22. Verse 20 itself carries an unresolved ketiv/qere crux: the consonantal ketiv שלשום against the pointed qere שָׁלִישִׁ֑ים (oshb:Prov.22.20, ketiv/qere, single-witness) leaves the numeral/rank term underlying 'thirty' versus an officer-class reading undecided by the bytes; this row reports the crux without resolving it. Prov.23.1 (web:Prov.23.1-Prov.23.1) opens an unrelated court-and-dining scenario sharing no skeleton token with 22:17-22:21, corroborating this unit's close at the 22:21 petuchah rather than continuing it.
